validated_results.title: Prediagnostic level of fatty acids in serum phospholipids: omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids and the risk of prostate cancer.
validated_results.reason: Nested case-control study of prediagnostic serum phospholipid omega-6 fatty acid levels and subsequent risk of incident prostate cancer, reporting a target-specific (null) association.

extraction.comparison_type: Increasing quartiles of serum phospholipid fatty acid levels
extraction.population: Blood donors to the Janus serum data bank who later developed prostate cancer, matched to blood donors without prostate cancer

cases.excerpt: Blood donors to the Janus serum data bank in Norway, who later developed prostate cancer, were matched to blood donors without prostate cancer (141 matched sets); the proportional level of fatty acids measured before diagnosis in the donors' serum was examined.

effect_size.excerpt: There was no clear association between the risk effect of total omega-3 and total omega-6 fatty acids.

comparison.excerpt: Increasing risk for prostate cancer was found with increasing quartiles of palmitoleic, palmitic and alpha-linolenic acid.

design.excerpt: The risk of later prostate cancer was analysed by conditional logistic regression.

timing.excerpt: the proportional level of fatty acids measured before diagnosis in the donors' serum was examined
